digest.component_or_area: snapshot janitor and review-bot storage management
propositions: The snapshot janitor's reclaim trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB free-space floor that is disk-size-blind, crossing the alarm threshold only at 93.3% on a 30 GiB volume, above the 85% alarm floor and the observed 90% peak.
Every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB / 69,984-file copy of the ticket tree on a cache key that advances every ~26 seconds with no reuse, producing ~4.4 GiB/h disk growth on the root volume.

The snapshot store sits on the container's writable layer because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, causing store_root() to fall through to tempfile.gettempdir() on the root disk instead of a dedicated volume.
The 7-day cold-trim threshold exceeds the container's lifetime (23 recreations in 4 days), and the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass.

A volume-relative headroom term with hysteresis must be added to the janitor's free-space trigger, evaluated as the maximum of the absolute floor and a percentage of total disk, so reclaim engages before the alarm threshold on any volume size.
